newsitem.title: UK: Horse Racing-Ireland's Dorans Pride less than cert.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Ireland's Dorans Pride less than cert.

text.p: Irish trainer Michael Hourigan said on Wednesday that Dorans Pride was less than certain to run in Thursday's Gold Cup after the going at Cheltenham racecourse was declared good-to-firm.
Hourigan said at the weekend that he would not risk his 6-1 chance stable-star if the ground was too firm on the day.
"I am worried about the ground. He will be declared but the decision will be taken as late as possible," Hourigan said.

Earlier, Philip Arkwright, clerk of the course at Cheltenham, said that having walked the entire course at 1145 GMT on Wednesday it was clear that the ground had dried up more than had been anticipated.
Irish entries fill the first three spots in the ante-post betting for the Cheltenham Gold Cup with the 1996 champion Imperial Call quoted 5-1 favourite and Danoli at 6-1.
Meanwhile, Aidan O'Brien-trained Istabraq has been backed down from 6-4 to 5-4 favourite in the betting shops at Cheltenham ahead of Wednesday's Sun Alliance Novices' Hurdle at 1400 GMT.
Klairon Davis, trained by Arthur Moore in County Kildare is generally available at 2-1 to retain his Queen Mother Chase title at 1435 GMT.
The Irish, who landed a record seven wins at the 1996 Festival, are still awaiting their first win in this year's campaign.
